prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

A Payment inside the `RawTransactions` of a Batch now follows the `DeliverMax` rule on output and input, like a top-level Payment. `simulate` and `submit` with `tx_blob` follow it too.

- `insertDeliverMax` applies the rule to each inner Payment of a Batch, so every method that already calls it renders inner Payments with `DeliverMax`. `simulate` and `submit` with `tx_blob` now call it on the `tx_json` they return.
- `removeDeliverMax` replaces the alias handling in `checkPayment`, maps `DeliverMax` to `Amount` in inner Payments as well, and runs before `checkFee` (and before `autofillTx` in `simulate`).

Fixes #8557

## Context of Change

`insertDeliverMax` only acted on a top-level `ttPAYMENT`, and `checkPayment` only aliased a top-level Payment. `DeliverMax` is not an `SField`, so `STParsedJSON` rejected it in an inner Payment as an unknown field. While tracing the callers I found that `simulate` had no `DeliverMax` handling at all, and `doSubmit` rendered `tx_json` without calling `insertDeliverMax`.

The alias is resolved before `checkFee` because `getTxFee` parses `tx_json` to compute the fee. A Batch fee depends on its inner transactions, so an unresolved inner `DeliverMax` fails that parse and the autofilled fee falls back to the reference fee. `autofillTx` in `simulate` has the same dependency for a multi-signed Payment.

## API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [ ] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

In API version 2, inner Payments and the `tx_json` returned by `simulate` and by `submit` with `tx_blob` now carry only `DeliverMax`, not `Amount`, matching every other Payment in v2. API version 1 gains `DeliverMax` next to `Amount`. `DeliverMax` is now accepted where it was rejected. Entries are in `API-CHANGELOG.md`.

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

A top-level JSON array is the batch form the specification defines, accepted from API version 3. Each entry is a request in its own right, nesting its parameters as a lone request does and correlating by its own `id`. The answer is an array of one reply per entry at HTTP 200, as the `method: "batch"` form answers. All entries of one body must name the same `api_version`, or name none and inherit the body's, and a body whose entries name two different versions the server serves is refused whole. For a top-level array the first entry naming a served version of 3 or above decides the version, and for a `method: "batch"` body the first entry naming a served version does, wherever that entry sits; a `method: "batch"` body may also name the version at its own top level, which then decides. An entry naming a version the server does not serve beside one naming a served version is answered in place, in the body's envelope, with `-32606`. A batch holds at most 100 entries, in either form and at every API version: a body with more entries is answered HTTP 400 with `Batch has too many entries`, as a version 3 error object or as a plain text body below version 3, before any entry is dispatched. One body has one version, found wherever dispatch would find it, which is what lets the limit read one version.

Closes #7202.

## Context of Change

Refusing a mixed body is a break a version 1 or 2 client can see, recorded as such in `API-CHANGELOG.md`, with two more the changelog states. A `method: "batch"` body whose entries name different served versions is served today, each entry at its own version, and is refused from now on. A `method: "batch"` body naming at its own top level a version the server does not serve is refused with `invalid_API_version`, where it was served at version 1 as if it had named none. A `method: "batch"` body whose top level names a version its entries disagree with is refused, where the top-level value was ignored and each entry was served at the version it named. One whose entries agree, with each other and with any top-level version, and holds 100 entries or fewer keeps working. A body refused before it has named a version is answered as version 1, so neither a malformed `params` nor the first entry decides the shape of the refusal.

Five conditions reject a whole array: empty, over the limit, holding nothing that could be a request, naming no served version of 3 or above, and naming two different served versions across its entries. Four answer one specification error object with a null `id`, an array naming none; an array holding nothing that could be a request answers one such object per entry, as the specification shows. Each reaches every API version, since no earlier version accepts an array.

## API Impact

- [x] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

`X-User` and the forwarded-for address are assigned by the connection's header, so they belong to the connection rather than to one entry of a `method: "batch"` body. The loop clears them in place for an entry whose own role is neither identified nor proxied, and a `std::string_view` shortened in place stays shortened, so the first such entry decides them for every entry after it. A later entry's role is read from that same value, so it is demoted along with the username.

Closes #7502.

## Context of Change

Read them into two entry-scoped views instead and hand those to the handler's context, so the clearing reaches only the entry it belongs to. A lone request is unaffected, there being no entry after it.

What a client can observe: a body whose first entry presents admin credentials made the second report no username, where the same entry sent alone reports the connection's. Every entry of one body now reports the role and username it would report alone.

## API Impact

None. No public API method, `libxrpl` interface or peer protocol message changes in this PR.

Remove the per-insertion heap allocations from `Batch::preflight`. The duplicate-inner-transaction and duplicate-sequence/ticket checks used an `std::unordered_set` and an `std::unordered_map` of `std::unordered_set`s; they are now `std::flat_set`s backed by a `boost::container::small_vector` sized to `kMaxBatchTxCount`, so neither container ever leaves inline storage.

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds the `BatchV2` amendment and a `ttBATCH_RESULT` (`BatchResult`) pseudo-transaction. When a `Batch` applies with `tesSUCCESS` in a closed ledger, `applyTransaction` inserts a `BatchResult` right after the batch's inner transactions. It carries the outer's ID in `sfParentBatchID` and lists every inner transaction the batch attempted, in order, as `sfTransactionHash` and `sfEngineResultCode`.

## Context of Change

An inner transaction that fails with a `tem`, `tef` or `ter` code leaves nothing in the ledger, and neither does any inner transaction of a rolled-back `tfAllOrNothing` batch. The outer's metadata covers only its own fee and sequence, so the only record of what a batch did is the `BatchTrace` log line on the node that applied it. #8164 keeps those results in a node-local table; this puts them in the ledger, so every node, Clio and explorer reads the same answer.

The record cannot be agreed in the transaction set like `ttFEE` or `ttAMENDMENT`, because its content exists only after execution. It is generated during the ledger build, as the inner transactions already are, from the outer ID and the inner IDs and results only, so every node produces the same leaf. It is inserted into the view the outer applied to, after the batch view is committed or dropped, so a rollback cannot remove it. The alternative was a field in the outer's metadata, but the outer's leaf is inserted before its inner transactions run and `OpenView::rawTxInsert` does not replace a leaf.

An entry was applied when its result is `tes` or `tec` and the batch was not rolled back; an inner transaction missing from `sfBatchResults` was never attempted. `sfEngineResultCode` is `INT32` because `tem`, `tef` and `ter` codes are negative.

`isPseudoTx` covers the new type, so it cannot be submitted or relayed, and `Change` preflight rejects it with `temINVALID` on any view, including from a proposed transaction set. Ledger replay skips it, and replaying the outer regenerates it.

## API Impact

- [x] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

`tx`, `ledger` and the transaction streams return the new `BatchResult` transaction type once `BatchV2` is enabled.

## Future Tasks

- Amend XLS-0056 to specify `BatchResult`.

## High Level Overview of Change

Mask `secret`, `seed`, `seed_hex`, and `passphrase` fields when HTTP batch RPC requests are rejected before handler execution. Masking traverses nested objects and arrays so sensitive values are not echoed in error responses or debug reply logs.

Closes #7461.

## Context of Change

The normal RPC handler-error path masks sensitive fields before attaching request data to an error response. Eight early-error paths in HTTP batch processing instead copied the request item directly into the response, bypassing that masking.

This change applies masking only to the copied request data used by those error paths. It leaves the original request available to subsequent processing and does not sanitize successful handler output, which can legitimately contain generated wallet credentials.

## API Impact

This is a non-breaking public API bug fix. The affected error responses preserve their existing structure, codes, messages, IDs, and non-sensitive request fields; only sensitive field values are replaced with `<masked>`. `API-CHANGELOG.md` documents the change.

## Before / After

Before, an early failure such as an invalid `api_version`, forbidden method, overload, malformed method, malformed `ripplerpc`, or non-object batch item could echo sensitive request values verbatim.

After, sensitive fields in the echoed request copy are masked recursively. Other batch items continue to execute normally unless the client is already over the resource limit.
